subject: Slab pricing & per-feature chargeback — next steps and economics
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Priya Mehra <priya.m@healytics.ai>; Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-08T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Slab pricing & per-feature chargeback — next steps and economics

Hi Priya / Sanjay —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we have alignment before Ben pulls together a formal proposal: 

1) Usage profile you shared (today + expected in 12 months):
   - Active users: 120k monthly active users (MAU) today, target 300k in 12 months.
   - Feature set: 3 primary inference features (SmartSummary, ClinicalTagger, InsightSynth).
   - Average per-session tokens: 1,200 tokens for SmartSummary, 650 for ClinicalTagger, 2,800 for InsightSynth.
   - Estimated blended monthly tokens (current / target): ~80M / ~240M.

2) Budget and commercial signals you gave:
   - FY28 inference budget range (team-level): $12k — $28k / month initially, flexible with committed volumes.
   - Target sensitivity: Priya mentioned a target of ~$900–$1,200 per 1M tokens as a starting benchmark for proof-of-concept.

3) Key commercial asks from your side:
   - Break down cost per feature (how slab pricing maps to each feature in a multi-feature deployment).
   - CAC payback sanity-check: example calculation if Healytics monetizes SmartSummary at $3.50 / user and targets 5–6 month CPC payback.
   - Margin headroom: we need to show gross margin sensitivity vs inference cost per feature so the PMs can model pricing tiers.

Next steps I propose (action owners):
   - Ben: build a slab pricing proposal with explicit per-feature chargeback examples + 3-tier commit options (trial, scale, enterprise). Attach a worked example spreadsheet. (Ben — can you target EOD Tue?)
   - Priya / Sanjay: share a simple sample prompt mix or a small usage CSV (1 week) so we can validate per-token distribution across features.
   - Logan: prepare a short margin sensitivity table (3 scenarios) and a one-page CAC payback example to share with your PMs before procurement.

Attachment: I will ask Ben to share the spreadsheet; for now, see rough numbers in-body below.

Rough blended checks (very rough):
   - If we price at $1,000 / 1M tokens, 240M tokens/month -> $240k / month (hosted) before any committed discounts — obviously we would structure reserved capacity to get unit economics into the $200–$120 / 1M effective cost to you.
   - If InsightSynth dominates tokens (as you said ~60% of heavy sessions), we should show per-feature effective cost by allocating tokens by feature usage mix.

I’ll loop Ben in to produce the concrete slab proposal and the worked CAC/payback table. Thanks again, and happy to jump back on a quick 20-min sync if you want to walk the spreadsheet together.

—
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Priya Mehra <priya.m@healytics.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Slab pricing & per-feature chargeback — next steps and economics

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. A few clarifications and a couple of numbers from our side: 

- The 240M figure is our Year+12 projection assuming successful rollouts across two pilots; pilot month expected token volume is closer to 35–50M.
- Feature split (pilot expected): InsightSynth ~55%, SmartSummary ~30%, ClinicalTagger ~15%.
- Pricing target: we are trying to get unit cost under $1,100 / 1M tokens for the pilot to keep our feature-level margins healthy; post-commit we can discuss steeper discounts.

Questions for Ben:
- Can you show a three-slab example where slab A (0–50M) is higher per-1M, slab B (50–200M) steps down, and slab C (200M+) is enterprise reserved pricing?
- For per-feature chargeback, we need sample allocation logic (e.g., allocate shared KV caching cost proportionally to token share vs flat per-feature uplift).

I’ll fetch a one-week extract of anonymized session-level token counts and share by EOD. Also looping in our procurement lead Sanjay (cc) — Sanjay, can you flag any standard SS&C (security, subscription, compliance) items we’ll need early?

Thanks,
Priya
Head of AI, Healytics
pri.mehra@healytics.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Mehra <priya.m@healytics.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healytics.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Slab pricing & per-feature chargeback — next steps and economics

Priya / Sanjay — attaching a first-pass slab proposal and a worked example that maps per-feature costs to the usage mix you shared. Highlights in the attachment: 

- Three-tier commit structure: Trial (0–50M), Growth (50–200M), Enterprise (200M+). Each tier has a per-1M list rate and an example committed discount for a 12-month reserve.
- Worked example tab: takes your pilot mix (InsightSynth 55 / SmartSummary 30 / ClinicalTagger 15) and shows per-feature monthly charge at list vs committed discount.
- CAC payback sheet: sample LTV assumptions + unit economics showing how SmartSummary priced at $3.50 / act user yields ~5.2 months payback under the Growth slab at 100M tokens.
- Margin sensitivity: shows gross margin at per-feature product prices vs Redwood cost per token (three cost scenarios: hosted list, reserved mid, reserved heavy quantized).

Attachments: healytics_slab_pricing_proposal.xlsx (contains: slab_pricing, worked_example, cac_payback, margin_sensitivity)

Quick notes:
- For allocation we recommend token-share proportional allocation for pure inference cost and a small flat allocation for non-linear KV/cache infra since it doesn’t scale linearly per request. We include both methods in the sheet so your finance team can pick the preferred model.
- If you want a simple export that maps session ids -> feature -> tokens for chargeback, we can provide a CSV once you sign a pilot NDA/PO.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

[Attachment: healytics_slab_pricing_proposal.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Priya Mehra <priya.m@healytics.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-10T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Slab pricing & per-feature chargeback — next steps and economics

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Ben — and thanks Priya for the prompt clarifications. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

- Priya / Sanjay: please send the one-week anonymized token extract (CSV) by Thu 11/11 so Ben and I can validate the slab mapping against real session mixes.
- Ben: finalize the proposal doc and add an appendix with a one-page procurement checklist (SOC2 evidence links, standard contract redlines, PO instructions). Can you have the updated deck by Fri 11/12?
- Logistics: suggested pilot: 3 months, with an optional convert-to-reserved clause at month 2 if utilization >75% of pilot commit. Also propose a 30% onboarding credit to offset initial dev/validation costs for our side.

I'll also drop a short one-page CAC/payback note (PDF) into the Drive folder and send a HubSpot update (deal HLT-2027-0421) with the pilot scope so procurement has one place to review. If procurement is green, Ben — can you prepare an initial SOW + PO template to accelerate execution?

Thanks all — happy to set a 20-min review once we have the CSV and the updated proposal.

—
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

[Links appended: HubSpot deal, Drive folder, DocuSign sandbox for NDA template]
